target.description: Seven-round AES-192/256, Figure 6 and Section 6 boundary convention. The explicit algorithm isolates sixteen bytes across k0, k1 and k7, not an explicitly budgeted full master key.

setting.key_relation: One unknown standard AES master key with its expanded round keys.
setting.plaintext_model: Generate N=2^78.5 limited-birthday pairs, requiring about 2^99.8 Q2 permutation queries. Section 3.3 permits input structures or inverse output structures.
assumptions: Q2 coherent secret-key oracle and QRAQM access are required; this is not a Q1 attack.
QRAQM random access is treated as an elementary unit operation; no physical-memory or gate-implementation estimate is claimed.
The search targets one surviving 128-bit subkey tuple. No quantitative full-master-key completion cost is supplied in Section 6.
Actual firstthree filter probabilities are2^-16,2^-16,2^-24; final stage combines two8-bit tests. Table4label discrepancy retained. StandardEq16 and optimizedEq17 are distinct.

success.description: Section4.1 explicitly separates success conditional on a unique surviving boundary-subkey tuple and bounded tables from the unquantified probability that those hypotheses hold. Q2 pair generation and full AES192/256 master-key completion are not quantified by this statement. Existing byte-index, table-label and memory conflicts remain; optimized Lemma4 has a further distinct-pair coverage gap, so its search-count tail is not a table-completion probability. The aggregate no-wrong-tuple bound below concerns the initial pair-table model only and does not quantify the complete recovery algorithm.

Eq5 gives the per-wrong-tuple survival model after N distinct valid pairs. The source AES assignment is N approximately2^78.5. The model's pair-survival independence is not proved for actual AES; the appended aggregate component applies a union bound without assuming independence between different wrong tuples.
Section4.4: the stated single-search bound requires the true marked fraction in[a/2,3a/2] and the source search choice. Not all distinct pairs, table completion or recovery.

Lemma4 Chernoff tail for the NUMBER of successful searches only, under the author independent-search model. Repeated successful samples can be duplicates; the existing coverage conflict is not resolved or hidden.

Union bound from Eq5 and Section6, given N distinct valid generated pairs and the source per-wrong-tuple survival model. N is the integer pair count, with source assignment N approximately2^78.5; the plug-in lower bound is approximately0.8325, not an exact probability for a rounded exponent. No independence between different wrong tuples is required. Independence across pair-survival tests is inherited from Eq5, not established for actual AES. This event does not include pair generation, correct-tuple retention, intermediate-table bounds, exact-oracle validity, optimized distinct-pair coverage or AES192/256 master-key completion. It is not end-to-end recovery success.
